annotation.title_clean: Wearable Four Degree of Freedom Upper-Limb Soft Robotic Rehabilitation Device, Disney Doesn't Care: Analyzing Ethical Failures in the AI Replication of James Earl Jones's Voice Through Care Ethics
annotation.title_en: Wearable Four Degree of Freedom Upper-Limb Soft Robotic Rehabilitation Device, Disney Doesn't Care: Analyzing Ethical Failures in the AI Replication of James Earl Jones's Voice Through Care Ethics
annotation.venue: University of Virginia Libra (Online Archive of University of Virginia Scholarship)
annotation.summary_en: University of Virginia undergraduate capstone abstract combining a technical project (wearable four-degree-of-freedom soft robotic exoskeleton for stroke upper-limb rehabilitation) with an STS paper applying care ethics to Disney's AI replica of James Earl Jones's voice in Fortnite. Full text is restricted; only the abstract is available.
key_provisions_or_claims: Care ethics applied to Disney's AI voice replica of Darth Vader in Fortnite shows lack of responsibility toward consumers and SAG-AFTRA.
Soft robotic exoskeleton offers a lightweight, inexpensive, home-based stroke rehabilitation option.
Engineers should design with user needs, safety and comfort in mind and speak up about safety concerns.
Companies have a duty of attentiveness and responsiveness to users.
